Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: pass: The mug is visibly to the right of the headphones. fail: The mug is visibly not to the right of the headphones. unknown: Their relative positions cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Inspect the edited image and compare the mug’s position with the headphones; this directly tests the requested outcome.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the mug is visibly to the right of the headphones.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague to reliably track the requested mug across the edit: the source has one blue mug left of the headphones, while the edited image appears to contain two mugs and a blue blur/ghost at the source location. Do not infer completion merely because a mug is now right of the headphones or because its position changed. Make the decision depend on identifying the original mug across source and edited images and assessing whether that object was moved to the right; distinguish a genuine moved mug from a duplicate, replacement, or residual blur. Preserve the rubric’s partial-progress distinction: evidence that the original mug moved toward the target but completion is not established supports partial, whereas uncertainty about object identity or the edit should remain unresolved rather than being converted to yes or no. The trace’s two high-confidence pass observations assert the target relation and change but do not resolve this identity/duplication ambiguity, so avoid treating their agreement as independent proof. No transport or schema failure is indicated; the mismatch is semantic/evidential.
s2: The binding should explicitly track the source’s single blue mug across the edit, using its distinctive color, shape, and handle as identity cues, rather than treating any mug now right of the headphones as the original. The edited image appears to show two smaller mugs and a blue blurred remnant near the source location; the trace’s high-confidence claim that a mug is right of the headphones does not establish that the original mug was moved, nor distinguish movement from duplication or replacement. Make the node assess whether the identifiable original object changed position relative to the headphones, and report only observable progress; leave identity or edit ambiguity unresolved. Keep this as a progress check, not a completion judgment: the aggregate rubric distinguishes partial progress from complete fulfillment, and this node alone should not force either label. The mismatch is semantic/evidential, not a transport or schema failure.
